q: what is kestrel?
a: Kestrel is an AI stock-trading bot that runs on your own Mac, with a normal Mac app window (its own window, Dock icon and menus) to watch it. It trades through Alpaca now, with Charles Schwab and Webull as other broker choices. It works as two "desks": a swing desk that holds for days to weeks and a day desk that's in and out the same day, each with $500. The plan is careful: study the market, write a plan, prove it with paper (pretend) money, and only then trade real money, capped at $1,000. The "AI" is a machine-learning model on your Mac, not a paid service. It isn't financial advice.
source: README.md (top, The app); trader/README.md (intro, desks table)

q: so what does this app actually do, does it trade for me automatically
a: Yes, once the autopilot is on, but in stages. First it studies and practices with pretend money. In Setup, the Start Stage 1 paper trading button lets the swing desk paper trade the momentum method right away; it decides 15 minutes before each close. Real money only comes after at least 30 trading days of paper results that pass your rules (made money, beat the S&P 500, never dropped more than 10% from its best day), plus a typed confirmation in the full Setup menu. The window shows your account against the S&P 500, positions, every trade and why, and has Pause and Emergency stop buttons.
source: README.md (Install step 5, The app); trader/README.md (The journey, Stage 1 shortcut); trader/config.yaml (promotion)

q: is kestrel made by schwab or alpaca? will it ask for my brokerage password
a: No. Kestrel is its own app with its own design, not a copy of Schwab's or Alpaca's, and it never shows or asks for your broker login. Alpaca connects with API keys you paste into Setup. For Schwab, you sign in on Schwab's own page that Setup opens, then paste the address your browser lands on. The app window itself only reads the bot's own files and holds no broker keys. Every key is saved only on your Mac, in ~/AITrader/.env.

q: how do i install kestrel on my mac
a: It takes about 3 minutes. 1) Click the Download Kestrel for Mac link at the top of the GitHub page and open Kestrel-mac.zip (it unzips itself). 2) Drag Kestrel into your Applications folder; it must live there to update itself. 3) Open it. The first time, macOS blocks it because it isn't from the App Store, so use Open Anyway in System Settings → Privacy & Security. 4) The first time only, a Terminal window installs Python and the bot's libraries, about 2 minutes. 5) The dashboard then appears with the Setup screen on top.

q: mac wont let me open kestrel, it says it cant be checked for malicious software
a: That's expected the first time: the app isn't signed by Apple (that costs $99 a year), so macOS blocks it. Click Done, then open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down, and click Open Anyway next to Kestrel. You may need your Mac password. If you prefer Terminal, paste this instead: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Kestrel.app". Make sure Kestrel is in your Applications folder first, since it needs to be there to update itself.

q: is the update out yet? how do i check
a: In the menu bar choose Kestrel → Check for Updates…, or press Check for updates at the bottom of the Setup screen. If you're current it says "You're up to date". If there's a newer one it shows "Version X is available (you have Y)" with Install and Restart or Later. Your installed version appears at the top right of the Setup screen. Usually you don't need to check: while the app is open it looks for updates by itself when it opens and once a day.
source: mac/app/updater.swift (checkForUpdates, confirm); mac/app/main.swift (buildMenus); trader/aitrader/web/dashboard.html (Setup footer, setup-version); trader/README.md (Updating)

q: does kestrel update itself or do i have to download every new version
a: It updates itself. While the app is open (it can sit minimized), it checks its download page when it opens and once a day. When there's a newer version it downloads it, checks the download's fingerprint and signature, swaps itself and restarts, and a running background autopilot restarts on the new version. With paper trading only, this happens automatically. If real money is involved, it asks you first. It must be in your Applications folder to replace itself. Versions before 1.0.13 can't update themselves: download the zip once more by hand.

q: why did kestrel ask me before updating this time? it used to just install
a: It asks first whenever real money is involved, so new code never takes over real-money trading unannounced. That's the case when real-money trading is switched on in .env (LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true), a desk is trading real money, or a desk owns real shares or has real orders open. The prompt lists the reason. With paper trading only, it installs by itself. It also always asks when you use Check for Updates… yourself or have turned off Update Automatically.

q: will an update wipe my keys or settings
a: No. Updates never touch ~/AITrader/.env (your keys), your Setup settings in ~/AITrader/my_settings.json, or your Schwab and Webull logins in ~/AITrader/data/, and the bot's memory stays too. What an update can replace is config.yaml, the defaults file; your Setup choices are applied on top of it. If config.yaml changed, your old one is saved as config.yaml.before-<version> and the menu tells you. Only deleting the AITrader folder removes your keys and data.

q: got a popup saying the bot was updated but this window wasnt, what do i do
a: It means macOS didn't let the app replace itself in Applications (it has no paid Apple developer ID). The bot's own code was updated, so trading already uses the new version; only the window is older. To let the window update too, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → App Management and turn Kestrel on. The alert's Open App Management button takes you there. Or press Download and drag the new version into Applications. Later just closes the message.

q: can i turn off auto updates
a: Yes. In the menu bar, Kestrel → Update Automatically (asks first when real money is on) is a checkmark item; click it to switch it off. With it off, Kestrel still checks when it opens and once a day, but it always asks before installing, with Install and Restart or Later. Click it again to turn automatic updates back on. When real money is involved, it asks first either way.

q: how do i get back to the setup screen
a: Click the Setup button at the top right of the Kestrel window; clicking the autopilot status pill next to it opens Setup too. It only pops up by itself the first time, when no Alpaca keys are saved and the autopilot is off. Press Done to close it. For the full Terminal menu (plans, real money, Schwab), use Kestrel → Setup Menu (keys, plans, autopilot)…, press ⌘, (Command-comma), or press Full Setup menu… at the bottom of Setup.

The keys are saved only on your Mac, in ~/AITrader/.env, and a running autopilot restarts to use them.

q: where do i even get the alpaca keys from

q: how do i turn on the autopilot

q: if i quit the kestrel app does the bot stop trading
a: No. The autopilot is a separate background service, so closing the app window doesn't stop it. It keeps running while the Mac is awake and you're logged in, and starts again when you log in. To actually stop it, use Setup → 2. Autopilot → Turn off; to stop new trades without turning it off, use Pause. q: whats lid closed mode
a: It's Keep trading with the lid closed, under Setup → 2. Autopilot. Normally closing a MacBook's lid puts it to sleep, and the bot stops. With this on and the Mac plugged in, it stays awake with the lid closed, day and night, and the autopilot keeps trading. On battery it sleeps as usual, and with the lid closed Kestrel puts it to sleep right away, so it never runs hot in a bag. It asks for your Mac password once, and also sets a weekday 8:30am New York time wake-up as a backup.
source: trader/aitrader/lid_mode.py (header); trader/aitrader/web/dashboard.html (lid-row); trader/README.md (Keep the Mac awake)

q: can i close my laptop and still have it trade
a: Yes, if it's plugged in and you turn on Setup → 2. Autopilot → Keep trading with the lid closed. Then the Mac stays awake with the lid closed and keeps trading. On battery it sleeps as usual, so unplugged with the lid shut, it isn't trading. Other options: keep the lid open with the charger in, or use clamshell mode (lid closed with an external monitor and power). Lid-closed mode also sets a weekday 8:30am wake-up, but wake-ups with the lid closed aren't guaranteed, so plugged in and awake is the dependable setup.

q: why does lid mode need my mac password? is that safe
a: Only an administrator can switch macOS's sleep lock, so Kestrel asks for your password once. It adds one rule, /etc/sudoers.d/kestrel-lid, checked by visudo first so a broken rule never gets installed. The rule lets Kestrel run exactly three commands without a password: pmset -a disablesleep 1, pmset -a disablesleep 0 and pmset repeat cancel, nothing else. The same step sets the weekday 8:30am New York time wake-up. If you cancel the password prompt, lid-closed mode just isn't turned on.
source: trader/aitrader/lid_mode.py (header, admin_script, turn_on); trader/README.md (Keep the Mac awake)

q: apple menu > sleep isnt doing anything
a: That's lid-closed mode at work. While it's on and the Mac is plugged in, macOS's sleep lock is on, so Apple menu → Sleep does nothing. To sleep the Mac by hand, first go to Setup → 2. Autopilot and turn Keep trading with the lid closed off (turning the autopilot off also releases it). Then the Mac sleeps normally again, and closing the lid puts it to sleep. If macOS still shows the lock on, Kestrel tells you to run sudo pmset -a disablesleep 0 in Terminal.

q: whats the good faith violation protection thing in step 4
a: A good faith violation is buying with money from a sale that hasn't settled, then selling before it settles. Three in 12 months and Schwab limits the account to settled cash for 90 days. When cash rules are on (broker Schwab or Webull with account type Automatic, or account type Cash), the bot only spends settled money: sale money waits one business day, with bank holidays counted. Step 4 then shows "on" and your violations out of 3. With Alpaca it says "not needed", because Alpaca covers unsettled money itself.

q: what settings can i change in kestrel
a: Open Setup, expand Real money, Schwab, Webull and Claude (for later), and look under Settings: Broker for real money (Alpaca, Charles Schwab or Webull), Paper trading happens at, Most real money the bot may use ($), Account type, Paper (practice) money ($), Fractional shares, Don't buy right before earnings (swing desk), Scan all US stocks every day, and Let Kestrel read the news. Press Save settings. They're kept when the app updates, and a running autopilot restarts to use them.

q: how do i turn off fractional shares
a: Setup → Real money, Schwab, Webull and Claude (for later) → Settings → Fractional shares (Alpaca and the simulation) → Off: whole shares only, then press Save settings. With it on, the bot can buy parts of a share at Alpaca and in the simulation, at least $1 at a time, only for stocks Alpaca allows. Schwab and Webull are whole shares only either way, so pricey stocks are skipped there. A stock whose single share costs more than a position's budget gets a "too pricey" tag on the watchlist.

q: wheres the setting that stops it buying right before earnings
a: It's Don't buy right before earnings (swing desk) in Setup → Settings. On (skip the last 3 trading days) means the swing desk won't open a new position within 3 trading days of a company's earnings report, because a report can jump a stock 10-20% overnight, past its stop. What it already owns is kept. Dates come from Yahoo each morning. The honest trade-off: stocks have on average done slightly better around earnings, so this gives up a little of that for fewer big surprise losses. Pick Off to disable it.
source: trader/aitrader/web/dashboard.html (set-earn); README.md (No swing buys right before earnings); trader/config.yaml (earnings.days_before)

q: can i stop it scanning every stock or reading the news
a: Yes, both are in Setup → Settings. Scan all US stocks every day → Off (only the watchlist) makes the swing desk pick only from its watchlist. Let Kestrel read the news → Off stops the headlines. With news on, it reads Alpaca's feed (Benzinga) with your keys, or Yahoo's without, shows headlines next to stocks, and won't buy a stock with danger headlines in the last 3 days, like a share offering, bankruptcy or trading halt. News never makes it buy. Press Save settings after changing either.

q: what does 'paper trading happens at' mean
a: It picks where the pretend-money trading runs. Automatic (Alpaca paper if its keys are saved) is the default; you can also pick Alpaca paper account, Webull paper account, or Simulated on this Mac. A broker is only used when its paper keys are saved; otherwise it's simulated on your Mac. You can't switch while a desk still holds paper positions where it trades now: wait until they're sold (the day desk sells before each close), then switch and press Save settings.

q: how do i set how much real money it can use
a: In Setup → Real money, Schwab, Webull and Claude (for later) → Settings, type the amount in Most real money the bot may use ($); it accepts $10 to $100,000. Choose the broker in Broker for real money, then press Save settings. This only sets a limit; it doesn't switch real money on. A desk trades real money only after its paper results pass the rules, LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true is set, and you type the confirmation in the full Setup menu. Each desk also keeps its own $500 budget and never borrows.

q: how do i connect my schwab account
a: Setup → Real money, Schwab, Webull and Claude (for later) → Charles Schwab. From developer.schwab.com, paste your app's App Key, Secret and Callback address exactly as registered (for example https://127.0.0.1:8182, no slash at the end); add the account number only if you have several. Press Save Schwab keys, then Open Schwab login, sign in and approve. Your browser ends on a page that won't load; that's expected. Paste that page's whole address into The address you landed on, press Finish login, then Test Schwab. Log in about once a week: Schwab's limit is 7 days.

q: can kestrel use webull
a: Yes. Setup → Real money, Schwab, Webull and Claude (for later) → Webull. First apply on Webull's website (API Management → My Application; Webull reviews it in about 1-2 business days). Once approved, Generate Key, paste the App Key and App Secret, pick Paper (test) or Real money, and press Save Webull keys. Then approve Kestrel in the Webull app within 5 minutes (Menu → Messages → OpenAPI Notifications → newest message → Check Now → the text-message code). To paper trade there, set Settings → Paper trading happens at → Webull paper account.

q: how do i connect claude to kestrel
a: In Setup, open Real money, Schwab, Webull and Claude (for later) → Connect Claude and press Claude Code or Claude Desktop. q: on the positions tab what does the check mark next to the stop loss mean
a: The ✓ means a stop-loss order is resting at the broker for that position. Without it, the bot checks the stop itself every 5 minutes. Hover over the stop price to see how far below the buy price it sits. q: whats on the trades tab
a: Trades shows how the chosen account is doing. q: what is the new p&l calendar
a: It's the Profit & loss calendar on the Trades tab. Each weekday of the month shows the money made or lost on trades that finished that day, how many trades and how many won, and a Week column totals each week. A line above it sums the month: the total, up and down days, and the best and worst day. Blue is a gain and red a loss, and a deeper color means a bigger day for that month. Hover a day for details, click it for its trades, and use ‹ › for other months.

q: how can i see what i made on one specific day
a: Open the Trades tab and find the Profit & loss calendar. Use ‹ › to get to the month, then hover over the day for a quick summary (finished trades, how many won and lost, and the account value change) or click it. Clicking lists the trades that finished that day: the stock, desk, when and at what price it was bought, what it made or lost, and why it sold. If none finished, it tells you how much the account value moved because of stocks it still holds. The Day by day table below has every day's numbers too.

q: why is the calendar blue and red instead of green
a: Blue means a gain and red a loss, a pair that stays readable with color-blindness. Every day also shows its amount with a plus or minus sign, so you never have to rely on color alone. A deeper shade means a bigger day compared with the rest of that month. The legend under the calendar labels them Made money and Lost money.

q: calendar has finished trades and account value buttons, whats the difference
a: Finished trades, the default, counts only money made or lost on trades that closed that day, so a day without finished trades stays blank. Account value shows the whole account's change that day, which includes the moves of stocks it still holds. So a day can show a loss in Account value with no trades at all, because something it owns dropped. The week totals and the month line follow whichever one you pick.

q: what does the activity tab show
a: Activity is every buy and sell with the bot's reason. Each row has the Date, Action (Buy or Sell), Symbol, Desk, Qty, Price, Amount, Profit / loss for sales, and Why. Filter with All, Buys or Sells, and with Both desks, Swing or Day. It shows whichever account is picked at the top of the Summary tab. Click any symbol to see what the company is and what Kestrel knows about it.

q: whats in research & plans
a: It shows the longer-term picture. Stocks it likes is the daily scan of all US stocks, ranked by the past year's rise, with each stock's price, days on the list and latest news; new listings sit in a separate watch-only list. TJR's model (Stage 2) shows its history test against random buys. The Options-gap watcher is testing only and never trades. Then each desk gets a card with its study report card, its trading plan, and What it learned from its own trades, where a losing strategy goes to half size and then a pause.

q: what's the journal tab for
a: Journal has two parts. On top is the After-market report, with a date picker for the last week of reports. Below is What the bot did, and why: a time-stamped log of its recent actions and messages, like the daily check-in, trades, pauses, warnings and lessons learned. If something looks off, the journal usually says why. The first report shows up after the first close with the autopilot on.

q: how do i see the demo data
a: Choose View → Show Demo Data (made-up prices), or press ⌘D. It takes about a minute to build: made-up prices run through the bot's real code, including the study month, the plans and a few weeks of paper trading, so you can see every tab before the bot has traded. A DEMO banner stays at the top the whole time. Choose the same menu item again to switch back to your real data.

q: is the demo using my real account? will it mess anything up
a: No. Demo data lives in its own folder (data/demo) and your real data is never touched. The prices are made up (a random walk), and the banner says "Not your account." The Setup screen keeps working on your real setup even while the demo is showing. Turn the demo off with View → Show Demo Data again.

q: pause button vs emergency stop button, which one should i use
a: Pause means no new trades. Nothing is sold now: stop-losses keep protecting what the bot owns, and the day desk still sells before the close because it never holds overnight. Emergency stop cancels the bot's orders, sells everything the bot owns right away, and halts both desks; you have to type SELL EVERYTHING to confirm. Neither one touches your own investments. Use Pause when you just want it to stop buying, and Emergency stop when you want out now.
source: trader/aitrader/web/dashboard.html (dlg-pause, dlg-kill); trader/aitrader/app_api.py (pause_all, kill); trader/README.md (Two buttons)

q: how do i stop the bot right now
a: It depends what you want. To stop new trades but keep what it owns, press Pause at the top of the window and confirm; stop-losses keep working. To get out completely, press Emergency stop, type SELL EVERYTHING and press Sell everything and stop: it cancels the bot's orders, sells everything it owns and halts both desks. q: will the emergency stop sell stocks i bought myself
a: No. Emergency stop only cancels the bot's own orders and sells what the bot itself bought; your own investments are never touched. The bot only sells shares it bought, never buys a stock you already own in that account, and only cancels its own orders (with Alpaca, every bot order carries an aitrader- tag). q: whats in the after market report

q: when does the after market report come out and where do i find it

q: what commands does the telegram bot understand

q: can i do the emergency stop from my phone

q: could someone else message my telegram bot and control kestrel

Before pairing, anyone who writes just gets told to send /start with the pairing code; after pairing, messages from anyone else get no answer at all. q: how do i set up pushover

q: how much does pushover cost
a: The Pushover app is free for 30 days, then a one-time $4.99 per platform (iPhone/iPad, Android or Desktop). Sending is free up to 10,000 messages a month. Setup's step 5 tag shows how many Kestrel has sent this month out of 10,000, and near that limit only urgent alerts go out. If you'd rather not use Pushover, Telegram also delivers alerts, and Telegram is the only way to send Kestrel commands from your phone.

q: which pushover alerts make noise
a: Kestrel uses Pushover's priorities. Emergency (2): a real-money kill switch or emergency stop repeats every minute, for up to an hour, until you open it. High (1): anything urgent, like a pause, a kill switch or a !!! warning, sounds even in quiet hours. Normal (0): every buy and sell, the after-market report, phase changes and warnings. Quiet (-1): everything else it forwards, such as daily results and lessons learned, arrives with no sound.

q: what happens if i hit the pushover monthly limit
a: Kestrel keeps count of what it sends each month. Pushover's free sending limit is 10,000 messages a month, and once Kestrel has sent 9,500 it only sends urgent alerts (high and emergency priority), keeping the last 500 for those. Routine alerts like buys, sells and daily results are skipped until the next month. A skipped or failed alert never stops trading, and Telegram alerts aren't affected by this count.

q: can i see the kestrel dashboard on my iphone

Tailscale is a free private network between your own devices. 1) Install Tailscale on the Mac and the iPhone and log in to the same account on both. 2) Press Turn on in step 6. 3) Open the link Setup shows on your phone (Send the link to my phone sends it through Telegram), then Share → Add to Home Screen so it opens like an app. It works from anywhere, but the Mac serves it, so the Mac must be awake with the autopilot on.

q: is the phone screen thing safe, is my account on the internet now
a: It isn't on the open internet. Kestrel serves the phone screen only on the Mac's Tailscale address, never on your Wi-Fi or the internet, and Tailscale encrypts everything between your devices. Every request also needs Kestrel's access key, which is in the link from Setup and then remembered by the phone. The phone can only watch and use the safety buttons; keys and settings are changed on the Mac only.

q: what does my mac need to do to keep trading

On a MacBook, also check System Settings → Battery → Options → "Prevent automatic sleeping on power adapter when the display is off".

q: what if the mac goes to sleep while the bot owns stocks
a: There are backups, though staying awake is the dependable setup. Every real position has a stop-loss order resting at the broker. With lid-closed mode on, a weekday 8:30am New York time wake-up is also set, but wake-ups with the lid closed aren't guaranteed.

q: what time does kestrel trade each day
a: On weekdays, New York time, with the autopilot waking every 5 minutes: at 9:25am a morning check-in; at 9:35am the day desk picks today's stocks in play; while the market is open the day desk decides every 5 minutes and sells everything before the close; the swing desk decides once, 15 minutes before the close (3:45pm on a normal day), and watches its stop-losses every 5 minutes. After the close it studies (about 10 minutes later), runs the options-gap watcher, scans all US stocks, and writes the after-market report about 25 minutes after the close.

q: what local ai model does kestrel use
a: Google's Gemma 4 12B (gemma4:12b in Ollama), about an 8 GB download. It writes the plain-English parts: the plan, the after-market report's summary and the team's notes; it never decides trades. A Mac with less than 16 GB of memory uses the small Qwen3 4B (qwen3:4b, about 2.5 GB) instead, so the AI never slows down trading. Setup step 7 shows which one your Mac uses.

q: how do i turn on the local ai
a: Install Ollama (free) from ollama.com/download and open it once. Kestrel then downloads its model by itself the next time it writes something, or press Setup step 7 → Download the model now. Step 7 shows the download's progress and says ready when it's done. Until then the small model writes the summaries if it's already on your Mac; otherwise Kestrel uses plainer template text, and everything else works the same.

q: does the local ai send my data anywhere
a: No. It runs inside Ollama on your own Mac (it talks to localhost:11434), so your trades and notes never leave the computer. The only download is the model itself, once, from Ollama. It also never sees your keys, and it never decides trades.

q: can i see what the ai is thinking live
a: Yes: the Thinking tab. At the top it says what the autopilot is doing this moment (for example "A day-desk check: scoring 40 stocks with tjr_model") or when the next check is. Below, for each desk: its latest check's top scores as bars next to the buy line and the sell line, what it decided and why (or why it didn't buy), the team's notes (Scout, Analyst, Trader, Risk), how far each holding is from its stop-loss, and every check so far today. It refreshes every 5 seconds while you look at it, and works on the phone screen too.

q: why does the thinking tab say no check yet today
a: The desk hasn't made a decision yet today. The day desk checks every 5 minutes while the market is open (it starts after 9:30am New York time); the swing desk decides once a day at 3:45pm and only checks its stop-losses before then. If it still says so during market hours, look at the top line: the autopilot may be off or the Mac asleep (Setup step 2).

q: what does kestrel do on weekends
a: It practices. On Saturday and Sunday it replays real past trading days from the prices saved on your Mac, about 30 minutes per day, through each desk's own strategy, team and risk rules (accounts weekend-swing and weekend-day). It also runs a crypto experiment: $500 of pretend money at live crypto prices, a decision every hour, everything sold Sunday at 11:50pm. Watch both live in the Thinking tab. None of it counts toward Stage 1, real money, or what the desks learn from their own trades.

q: does weekend practice count toward stage 1
a: No. Stage 1's 30 days are real market days in the paper account. The weekend replay uses days that already happened, and the strategies were chosen by testing that same history, so its results aren't new evidence. The weekend accounts are kept apart from the in-its-head, paper and real ones, and the mistake memory never reads them. Each weekend starts fresh.

q: is the weekend crypto trading real
a: No: pretend money ($500) at real, live crypto prices from Alpaca's free crypto data. No order goes to any broker, so it can't mix with your Alpaca paper account's stocks. It uses the swing desk's momentum method on hourly bars, which was only ever tested on stocks, so treat it as an experiment. Turn it off in Setup → Settings → Weekend practice: crypto.

q: how do i turn off weekend practice
a: Setup → Real money, Schwab, Webull and Claude (for later) → Settings → Weekend practice: replay real past days, and Weekend practice: crypto, pretend money. Set either one to Off and press Save settings.
